valuation.method: Industrial gas company with a stable, profitable operating base: forward P/E on FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS, viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027). Single listing in USD (NYSE/Nasdaq common ordinary shares, 1:1, no depositary receipt, no FX conversion). Earnings base: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $17.82 to $17.92 (midpoint $17.87, +8% to +9%, including about 2% favourable currency) from the Q3 2026 release of 2026-10-29, with Q3 adjusted EPS $4.59 and Q4 guidance of $4.40 to $4.50. Base FY2027 EPS of $19.60 is +9.7% on the $17.87 midpoint and sits between the Erste estimate ($19.60) and the freshest aggregator consensus ($19.77, WallStreetZen). Share count: 459,083,779 ordinary shares at 2026-09-30 (10-Q cover), the same figure as the aggregate, so no dilution is assumed. Net debt is not needed for a P/E method; for reference total debt was $26,702m and cash $3,947m at 2026-09-30 (net debt about $22.8bn, derived). Bear: $18.50 x 22x = $407.00 (-22.6%); 22x is close to the 52-week low of $387.78 (about 21.7x FY2026 midpoint). Base: $19.60 x 27x = $529.20 (+0.6%). Bull: $20.50 x 30x = $615.00 (+16.9%). Dividend: $1.60 per quarter declared in Q2, Q3 and Q4 2026, so $6.40 a year as a gross expected cash dividend (6.4 / 526.06 = 1.2% yield).

bear.driver: Growth slows to the low end of FY2027 estimates as the Lincare drag (about 2% of EPS growth lost year to date) persists and project backlog conversion lags; the multiple de-rates toward the 52-week low.

base.driver: FY2027 EPS of $19.60 (+9.7%) on the FY2026 guidance midpoint with price and volume recovery and modest currency tailwind fading; multiple held near today's forward level of about 27x.

bull.driver: Backlog growth and productivity lift FY2027 EPS to $20.50, near the top of the published range, and the market keeps a quality premium of 30x as the industrial gas franchise re-rates.

valuation.implied_by_close: The close of $526.06 equals 26.8x base FY2027 EPS of $19.60 (29.4x the $17.87 FY2026 midpoint). The mean published target of $551.04 (S&P Global, 29 analysts via StockAnalysis) equals 28.1x base EPS, or EPS of $20.41 at 27x; the analysts' gap of about 4% above the base target is a multiple-and-EPS difference, and the analysts' assumptions are not sourced.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E on base EPS moves the base target by $19.60 (3.7 pp of the close). A $0.50 change in FY2027 EPS at 27x moves it by $13.50 (2.6 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Adjusted EPS growth against the 8% to 9% FY2026 guide and the FY2027 outlook, with the Lincare drag and currency tailwind disclosed; the base case needs roughly 9% to 10% EPS growth in FY2027 with the multiple held.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and full-year 2026 results with the FY2027 outlook, expected in February 2027 (exact date not confirmed; one aggregator lists 11 Feb 2027).

analyst_notes: Five named analysts have dated targets since Oct 30, 2026: BMO (McNulty) trimmed to $540 from $546 on Nov 3, while Goldman (Fischer) raised to $595 from $580 and Citi (Cunningham) raised to $580 from $560 after the Q3 print, and Wells Fargo (Eberts) set $570 on Oct 30 with no prior shown. Named targets average $570.60, about 8.5% above the $529.20 base case, and every named view is a Buy except DZ Bank's Hold (no target). The sample is partial and the post-earnings raises are concentrated in a few names; RBC raised to $568 from $549 and UBS to $585 from $574 on Oct 30 to Nov 2, but neither analyst is named in the sources, so they are excluded from the individual calculation. No named firm documents a 12-month horizon in the sources opened, so target rows are not in the weighted target and the sample is shown for timeline only.
